final_message:
I fixed `int_to_roman` in `src/roman.py`, and `int_to_roman(4)` now returns `'IV'`.

The function only had the symbols for 1, 5, 10, 50, 100, 500 and 1000, so it could never produce subtractive forms. I added 900 (`CM`), 400 (`CD`), 90 (`XC`), 40 (`XL`), 9 (`IX`) and 4 (`IV`) to the lookup table.

I checked it by round-tripping every number from 1 to 3999 through `int_to_roman` and then `roman_to_int`, and all of them came back unchanged. `int_to_roman(1994)` gives `'MCMXCIV'`. I didn't add a test file to the repo.
